 Judgment

In a road accident that took place at around 9.30 a.m, on 27.06.2017, a 52 year old Veerapathiran,
the claimant herein, suffered multiple injuries to his person, owing to the rash driving of the offending vehicle bearing registration No.TN19-AC-1802, which dashed against the victim's vehicle.
In particular, he suffered fractures to his left temporal bone, left shoulder, ribs and right femur.
He was hospitalised for 14 days, and also underwent multiple surgeries for correcting the fractures.
2. The victim of the accident approached the Tribunal with his claim for compensation.
At the instance of the Tribunal, the victim's disability was assessed by the medical board at 30%, and it issued Ext.C1, disability certificate for that purpose.

Acting on the same and awarding compensation at Rs.3,000/- for every percentage of disability, the Tribunal awarded Rs.90,000, and towards medical expenses, it had awarded Rs.2,79,512/- at actuals, and after providing other conventional heads of compensation, it awarded Rs.4,59,012/-, which was rounded off to Rs.4,59,050/-.

The details https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis are as below :

8 Loss of future prospects 30,000.00

Total :
4,59,012.00 (Rounded off to ) 4,59,050.00
Aggrieved by the perceived inadequacy of the compensation, the claimant approached this Court.

3. The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant was a coolie, that due to multiple fractures he had suffered, especially to his shoulder and limbs, he is not as fit as he was prior to the accident, and could not pursue his avocation.
He added in fitness of things, the Tribunal ought https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis to have treated his disability as functional disability.
He also submitted that the Tribunal was also parsimonious in granting compensation for other non- pecuniary, conventional heads of compensation.
4. The learned counsel for the second respondent-insurance company made his submissions justifying the quantum awarded by the Tribunal.
5. It is not in dispute that the victim of the accident was a coolie by profession, and his shoulders and legs are the main functional organs for pursuing his avocation.
When they are damaged, it is only reasonable to conclude that the disability he had suffered is functional.
Accordingly, this Court treats the disability suffered by the victim as functional disability, and fixes it at 15%.
So far as reckoning his income is concerned, in an accident that took place in 2017, the Tribunal had reckoned his monthly income at Rs.7,000/-, which does not have any relevance to reality.
This Court considers that Rs.12,000/- per month would be an appropriate notional income.

Taking Rs.12,000/- as monthly income, adding 10% towards future prospects and applying 11 as multiplier,
and reducing the sum arrived to 15%, this Court determines the compensation payable under the head o https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis functional disability at Rs.2,61,360/-.

So far as other D.Veerapathiran vs R.Nishanthan on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146814087/
2 conventional heads are concerned, this Court chooses to enhance it reasonably.

To conclude, the appeal is partly allowed, and the compensation is enhanced from Rs.4,59,050.00 to Rs.6,66,000/-.
It is informed that the second respondent-insurance company had already deposited the sum awarded by the Tribunal.

The second respondent is now directed to deposit the differential sum with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum, less any amount for the interest payable for 414 delay in filing the appeal, within a https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
The appellant is required to pay the necessary court fee, if any, for the enhanced amount.
No costs.
